corrected_verdict: RELATED_ONLY (unchanged). Add a maths precedent: the Equal-shares quantity and its averaging bound are classical cyclic-group-code facts (Slepian 1968, Theorem 2), and s=1 is Slepian's initial-vector problem, solved by the regular simplex.
issues: (1) PRIOR ART THE CHECKER MISSED (maths). Put energy y_j in rotation plane j. Then kappa_j(delta)=1-cos(2 pi j delta/p) gives ||X_delta - X_0||^2 = 2 sum_j y_j kappa_j(delta) for the cyclic group code X_delta = D(delta) X_0 of Slepian (BSTJ 47(4):575-602, 1968). Consequences: M_K(p) is half the squared minimum distance of the best equal-energy cyclic group code with frequency set S. The averaging bound M_K <= pK/(p-1) is Slepian's Theorem 2 (p. 591): sum_R d^2(X_R,X) = 2g for any unit X under a nontrivial real-irreducible representation. Gamma_1(p) = p/(p-1), with its flat maximizer, is Slepian's 'initial vector problem' for Z_p, solved by the regular simplex (relevant to item r8-dense-corollary). For s>1 the l_{1/s} budget is not an energy constraint, so the sparse programme itself is not covered. I verified this from the full BSTJ text on archive.org. Biglieri-Elia, IEEE TIT 22(5):624-629, 1976 (optimal frequency choice for cyclic group codes) exists per Crossref, but its content could not be fetched, so it is not recommended. (2) Checker's citations: both verified. neyshabur2015norm: PMLR v40 pp. 1376-1401, and the three quotes are verbatim in arXiv 1503.00036v2, Secs. 3.1-3.2. savarese2019infinite: PMLR v99 pp. 2667-2690, and it is relevant only to the ReLU paragraph. Caveat on Neyshabur: their norm is the per-layer group norm mu_{p,q}, and the Thm 3 construction adds an averaging layer (d>=3). The paper's norm is the per-neuron L_{2,b}. So phrase it 'cf. the unit-duplication argument of \citet{neyshabur2015norm}, Sec. 3.2', not 'the argument of'. The thresholds coincide at nu=2, p=2 (q<=p*=2 vs b<=nu=2). (3) The b>nu and b<2 facts are elementary l_r-norm facts (a spread vector has l_r norm H^{1/r-1}; the power-mean constant is |F|^{1-b/2}) and need no further citation. The arithmetic checks. (4) Minor: 0.408 equals 6^{-1/2} (0.40825) to 3 decimals, and 0.408/0.577 = 1/sqrt2. State it if exact, or give more digits. extra_citations.why: M_K(p) is half the squared minimum distance of an equal-energy cyclic group code with frequency set S. The averaging bound M_K <= pK/(p-1) is Slepian's Theorem 2 (distance sum 2g per nontrivial real-irreducible component, independent of the initial vector). At s=1 (b=nu) the programme is his initial-vector problem, whose optimum is the regular simplex, matching Gamma_1 = p/(p-1). Optional one-clause cite in the Equal-shares paragraph and the dense corollary.
